paragraphs: This paper develops a quantum framework for several regression problems, extending beyond the linear regression setting that has dominated earlier quantum work. Its scope includes Lasso, Ridge, Huber, and other regression families. The central claim is an improvement of up to a quadratic factor in how computation depends on the number of samples, relative to the best classical algorithms.

The method builds a quantum counterpart to a recent classical regression approach. It uses quantum approximations of leverage scores, which guide the selection of informative samples, to initialize and refine multiscale estimates. Preparing multiple copies of quantum states then supports importance sampling. These pieces form a complete computational pipeline rather than an isolated quantum subroutine.

The stated runtime depends on sample count, problem dimension, sparsity, and the requested error level. Its sample-dependent term scales with the square root of the sample count, while an additional term depends polynomially on dimension and inverse error. Consequently, the claimed acceleration concerns a particular complexity dependence; it does not imply an unconditional quadratic reduction in total runtime for every regression problem.
icml-2026-accelerating-regression-tasks-.tldr: A unified quantum regression framework offers up to quadratic improvement in sample-count dependence across several regression families.

paragraphs: AIR addresses the problem of choosing training examples that effectively transfer reasoning skills between language models. Common selection rules use properties such as response length, uncertainty, or overall prediction loss. The paper argues that these signals miss which individual reasoning steps depend most strongly on mechanisms important to reasoning.

The framework identifies reasoning-critical attention heads in an existing model, then constructs a weakened reference by disabling their influence. It measures the resulting divergence in prediction loss to produce an Attention Influence Score. This intervention supplies a mechanism-based signal for assessing both complete examples and individual steps within an example. The selection procedure itself is unsupervised and requires no training.

The scores support two uses: selecting samples for post-training and assigning different fine-tuning weights to reasoning steps. Experiments across several reasoning benchmarks report consistent accuracy improvements over heuristic selection methods and effective identification of important steps and samples. The contribution is a way to allocate training effort according to measured attention-head influence, connecting internal model behavior to practical data selection.
icml-2026-air-post-training-data-selecti.tldr: AIR selects and weights reasoning data by measuring how prediction loss changes when reasoning-critical attention heads are weakened.

paragraphs: This paper studies how to make regression models interpretable when features interact strongly. Explanations based on additive effects can lose information through cancellation or evaluate combinations outside the data's support. The proposed Tensor Separation Learning model instead represents predictions as a sum of products, with each product assembled from functions of individual features.

Those products preserve a structured way for features to interact while keeping their individual functions available for inspection. The model is built through a stagewise greedy procedure with orthogonal refitting. A central result is that first-order partial dependence functions can reconstruct the learned model up to constant factors. The correspondence holds stage by stage, making the resulting visualizations faithful to the fitted components.

The paper also establishes approximation-rate guarantees for functions whose mixed partial derivatives of the specified order are bounded. That condition defines the scope of the theoretical result. Regression experiments show performance competitive with black-box models. Together, the findings support separability as a route to combining interaction modeling with explanations that retain the structure of the fitted predictor.
icml-2026-beyond-additive-decompositions.tldr: Tensor Separation Learning models feature interactions through separable products while supporting faithful reconstruction from first-order partial dependence functions.

paragraphs: CamGeo tackles image-to-video generation when only a small number of camera poses are supplied. Sparse instructions leave much of the motion between specified views unconstrained. The paper identifies pose drift and discontinuous motion as problems in existing methods and attributes them to insufficient three-dimensional geometric guidance.

The framework transfers geometric knowledge from a pretrained video-to-3D model, VGGT, into the video diffusion backbone during training. One distillation component enforces cycle consistency between keyframe trajectories and the provided poses. Another applies camera-trajectory and depth constraints across frames, including those without direct supervision. Together, these objectives encourage generated views to describe a consistent underlying structure.

Training follows a three-stage curriculum that moves from overall geometric coherence toward finer refinement as complexity increases. Because the distillation machinery is used only during training, it does not add inference latency. Experiments report consistent improvements across different levels of pose sparsity. The approach therefore targets the missing geometric guidance between sparse camera instructions while preserving the inference-time generation pipeline.
icml-2026-camgeo-sparse-camera-condition.tldr: CamGeo distills 3D knowledge into a video generator during training to improve motion consistency under sparse camera guidance without adding inference latency.

paragraphs: ConvexBench tests whether language models can identify convexity in symbolic expressions built from deeply nested functions. Convexity recognition matters in optimization, control, and learning, but the paper focuses specifically on the challenge of following functional composition. The benchmark is scalable and mechanically verifiable, allowing expression depth to increase while answers remain checkable.

Tests of frontier models reveal a steep deterioration as nesting grows: reported F1 falls from 1.0 at depth 2 to roughly 0.2 at depth 100. Inspection of reasoning traces identifies parsing failures and what the authors call lazy reasoning. These findings distinguish trouble understanding the expression's structure from failures to work through its intermediate parts.

The proposed remedy divides the job into explicit stages. An external tool parses the expression into an abstract syntax tree, and an agent reasons recursively over each sub-expression using focused context. The framework substantially improves results on deep compositions, including a reported F1 of 1.0 at depth 100. This supports structured decomposition as an effective intervention in the evaluated setting.
icml-2026-convexbench-can-llms-recognize.tldr: ConvexBench exposes failures in recognizing convexity under deep composition and shows that external parsing plus recursive reasoning can substantially improve performance.

paragraphs: CoPE addresses a training problem for language-model agents: a long-term plan and the actions taken to execute it can fail to agree. A plan may be impractical, or an execution trajectory may depart from its intended direction. Training on such examples can propagate those weaknesses into the agent's planning and execution policies.

The framework makes planning–execution coordination an explicit part of optimization. It uses Self-Refining Monte Carlo Tree Search to generate plans and multiple execution trajectories through interaction with the environment. It then quantifies how well the plans and trajectories coordinate and gives greater optimization weight to samples with stronger agreement.

This changes which experiences have the greatest influence during fine-tuning. The agent learns more heavily from examples where planning and execution work together, addressing their relationship within the training process. Experiments on benchmarks containing two long-horizon, multi-step tasks report substantially improved coordination and performance above state-of-the-art baselines. The results support the value of optimizing this relationship explicitly for the evaluated agent tasks.
icml-2026-cope-a-framework-for-optimizin.tldr: CoPE improves agent training by giving more weight to experiences in which long-term plans and multi-step execution coordinate well.

paragraphs: DocOS examines how graphical-interface agents handle unfamiliar procedures that are absent from their learned knowledge. The paper argues that relying on pretraining or instruction tuning leaves agents vulnerable on these long-tailed tasks, often pushing them into brittle trial and error. It proposes that agents proactively seek documentation as part of solving the task.

The contribution is a benchmark for this document-guided behavior in fully interactive environments. Agents must operate a browser, find relevant online instructions, understand the procedure, and translate it into executable interface actions. This evaluates a connected process: locating useful knowledge and then applying it correctly within the environment.

Experiments identify two bottlenecks. Agents have difficulty reliably finding the relevant information during search, and they also struggle to turn retrieved instructions into precise actions. These findings indicate that access to documentation alone does not resolve the task. The benchmark makes both information acquisition and faithful execution visible as obstacles, providing a concrete setting for studying agents that adapt to unfamiliar procedures through external guidance.
icml-2026-docos-towards-proactive-docume.tldr: DocOS benchmarks agents that proactively find documentation and execute its instructions, revealing failures in both search and action grounding.

paragraphs: DCL-MVC aims to cluster examples described through multiple views into a shared grouping. Different views can contribute complementary information, but noise and differences between them can make fusion unreliable. A second problem arises near cluster boundaries, where uncertain assignment probabilities can lead to examples being placed in the wrong group.

The method introduces contrastive learning at two stages. During fusion, it first combines information and then applies attention to learn how much weight to give each view. An instance-level contrastive objective encourages representations of the same example across views to align. This stage targets the reliability of the shared representation before refining cluster structure.

During representation learning, a cluster-center contrastive loss increases separation between clusters, while prototypical contrastive learning encourages examples within a cluster to become more compact. A confidence-aware curriculum guides this process, with particular attention to uncertain boundary examples. Experiments on six real-world datasets report consistent gains over strong baselines and support the contribution of each component. The results connect improved cross-view fusion with more decisive cluster assignments.
icml-2026-dual-stage-contrastive-learnin.tldr: DCL-MVC uses contrastive learning during both multi-view fusion and cluster refinement to improve alignment and resolve uncertain assignments.

paragraphs: E-VAds studies video understanding in short e-commerce advertisements, where visual, spoken, and written information serve commercial goals. The paper introduces a framework for assessing multimodal information density and finds substantially higher density in this content than in mainstream datasets. This motivates evaluation that includes reasoning about commercial intent alongside perception.

The benchmark contains 3,961 videos from Taobao across varied product categories. A multi-agent system generated 19,785 open-ended question–answer pairs, organized into five tasks spanning perception, cognition, and reasoning. Its purpose is to test understanding of the dense, goal-driven content that general-purpose video benchmarks do not adequately capture.

The paper also develops E-VAds-R1, a reasoning model trained with reinforcement learning. Its MG-GRPO reward design supplies smooth guidance during early exploration and a nonlinear incentive for highly precise answers. Experiments report a 109.2% performance gain in commercial-intent reasoning using only a few hundred training examples. This is a reported improvement in that reasoning evaluation, rather than a claim about commercial outcomes or every aspect of video understanding.
icml-2026-e-vads-an-e-commerce-short-vid.tldr: E-VAds introduces a benchmark for dense e-commerce videos and a reinforcement-learning model that improves commercial-intent reasoning with limited training data.

paragraphs: This paper develops uncertainty estimates for geometric models that predict symmetric rank-2 tensors. Such a target has six Kelvin-Mandel coordinates, so its full uncertainty requires a 6-by-6 covariance matrix. The aim is to make both the predicted mean and its uncertainty transform consistently with rotations, while ensuring that every predicted covariance is positive definite.

The framework organizes covariance components using irreducible representations of rotational symmetry. It predicts in the space of symmetric matrices and applies matrix exponentiation to reach the space of symmetric positive-definite matrices. This construction strictly guarantees positive definiteness while maintaining exact equivariance, combining a valid covariance structure with the required geometric transformation behavior.

For training, the authors introduce a Log-Euclidean Equivariant Scoring Objective based on a multivariate Laplace distribution. The surrogate loss is designed for robustness to heavy-tailed errors and stable optimization. Evaluations on ModelNet40 inertia tensors and Materials Project dielectric tensors report competitive performance and physically consistent uncertainty estimates, with useful sensitivity to risk and out-of-distribution inputs. Those empirical properties complement the construction's structural guarantees.
icml-2026-equivariant-covariance-tensors.tldr: The framework produces symmetry-preserving tensor uncertainty with guaranteed positive-definite covariance matrices and empirically useful risk sensitivity.

paragraphs: Language-model parameter editing often starts by computing a desired internal hidden state at an anchor layer. To coordinate edits across several layers, existing methods commonly distribute that target backward to preceding layers. This paper systematically investigates the basis of that practice, examining its capability boundaries, practical considerations, and potential failure modes.

The proposed alternative changes where the anchor is placed and how other targets are obtained. It optimizes the target at the first editing layer, then propagates that state forward through the model. Subsequent editing layers receive targets derived from this forward computation, producing layer-specific hidden states that are mutually compatible with the propagated anchor.

The paper reports more accurate targets with the same computational complexity as existing approaches. The change leaves the initial hidden-state target computation and the other components of the editing pipeline intact, making it applicable to a wide range of parameter-editing methods. Its contribution is specifically a revised construction of coordinated layer targets, grounded in the model's forward propagation rather than a backward distribution of a later-layer target.
icml-2026-from-backward-spreading-to-for.tldr: Forward replay constructs more accurate, compatible editing targets by optimizing an early-layer anchor and propagating it through subsequent layers.

paragraphs: GAE addresses the gap between a vision-language model's high-level planning and the precise actions a robot must execute. The paper argues that entangling reasoning with action generation can restrict generalization and make adaptation costly. Its solution separates these responsibilities through a sparse geometric interface shared by a planner and an action expert.

The vision-language model predicts a small set of three-dimensional waypoints expressing its intended motion. GAE combines these waypoints with current point-cloud observations to produce continuous action trajectories. The expert is pretrained on 150,000 trajectories from simulated and real robots. An Action Pre-training, Pointcloud Fine-tuning scheme further separates learning action dynamics from grounding actions in geometry.

After pretraining, GAE remains frozen and is reused across downstream tasks. Adaptation requires only lightweight fine-tuning of the vision-language model to produce the waypoint interface. Experiments report strong performance and generalization across visual domains, camera viewpoints, and language instructions. These findings support the usefulness of a reusable action component connected to task reasoning through an explicit geometric representation.
icml-2026-gae-unleashing-physical-potent.tldr: GAE turns sparse 3D plans into continuous robot actions through a reusable action expert that stays frozen across downstream tasks.

paragraphs: GeoSense targets limited spatial understanding in multimodal language models. Geometric information can help, but supplying it for every input adds computation even when ordinary image cues may suffice. The paper therefore focuses on teaching a model to recognize when its available visual evidence is insufficient and additional geometry is needed.

The framework first adds an independent channel for geometric features and uses alignment training so the model can make effective use of them. It then applies supervised fine-tuning with a specially curated spatial-awareness dataset. This second stage is intended to activate internal cues that let the model determine when to engage geometric information during reasoning.

The resulting approach combines access to geometry with a learned decision about its necessity. Experiments across multiple spatial-reasoning benchmarks report significant spatial gains without compromising two-dimensional visual reasoning. These findings support selective use of geometric features in the evaluated tasks. The paper's notion of perceptual awareness concerns this specific judgment about insufficient input cues and the need for geometry within the reasoning process.
icml-2026-geosense-internalizing-geometr.tldr: GeoSense teaches multimodal models to engage geometric features when 2D cues are insufficient, improving evaluated spatial reasoning without harming 2D performance.

paragraphs: HiDe revisits why multimodal language models struggle with high-resolution images. While zooming is often motivated by difficulty recognizing small objects, the paper's analysis identifies background interference as the dominant failure mode. This shifts the focus toward selecting relevant regions and removing distracting context while preserving useful spatial relationships.

The training-free framework first separates the contributions of question tokens and identifies the most informative ones. Their attention patterns guide the selection of visual regions. A second stage extracts those regions from clutter and builds a compact representation that retains key layout information. In this way, attention becomes an explicit mechanism for choosing what visual evidence the model sees.

HiDe reports state-of-the-art high-resolution benchmark results, including 92.1% for Qwen2.5-VL 7B and 91.6% for InternVL3 8B on Vstar Bench, surpassing reinforcement-learning-based methods there. After optimization, it also reduces memory usage by 75% relative to the previous training-free approach. These results support the paper's emphasis on reducing distracting background while keeping the spatial structure needed for the question.
icml-2026-hide-rethinking-the-zoom-in-me.tldr: HiDe uses question-guided region selection and layout-preserving background removal to improve high-resolution visual reasoning without training.

paragraphs: LieStoNet discovers continuous symmetries in stochastic differential equations directly from observed trajectories. Such symmetries describe transformations compatible with the dynamics and can make scientific models more interpretable. The framework does not require a predefined symmetry group, template, or canonical coordinate system, addressing settings where the relevant transformations are initially unknown.

It first learns neural approximations of drift and diffusion from trajectory increments. It then learns projectable symmetry generators by enforcing the equations that characterize SDE Lie-point symmetries. Separate regularizers encourage closure under Lie brackets, compliance with Lie algebra axioms, and an independent, nonredundant basis. These constraints organize candidate generators into an interpretable algebraic structure.

The learned dynamics also define an associated Fokker–Planck equation, whose Lie-point symmetries can optionally be discovered in parallel. Tests on several canonical SDEs with known analytic symmetries recover generators consistent with the ground-truth symmetry algebras. This provides evidence for recovering interpretable structure from noisy dynamics in those systems, without requiring the symmetry family to be specified beforehand.
icml-2026-liestonet-learning-lie-symmetr.tldr: LieStoNet learns continuous symmetries of stochastic dynamics from trajectories without prespecifying symmetry groups or templates.

paragraphs: MOD-DiT targets the high cost of self-attention in video diffusion transformers, where long sequences make full attention expensive. Sparse attention reduces the connections being computed, but fixed patterns can miss changing dependencies. Existing dynamic approaches can also spend substantial computation repeatedly sampling to determine which attention connections to retain.

The proposed framework predicts evolving sparse patterns without those sampling operations. It uses information from early denoising steps and a distributed mixing approach to build an efficient linear approximation. That approximation predicts attention masks for a particular denoising interval. An online block-masking strategy then applies the predictions while retaining historical information about sparsity.

This two-stage design makes adaptation depend on learned approximations of attention behavior and accumulated sparsity information. Its purpose is to keep the selected connections responsive to generation while avoiding repeated sampling overhead. Evaluations across multiple benchmarks and model architectures report consistent acceleration and improved generation quality. The findings support dynamic mask prediction as a practical way to improve both efficiency and output quality in the evaluated video generators.
icml-2026-mixture-of-distributions-matte.tldr: MOD-DiT predicts dynamic sparse attention masks from early denoising information, improving evaluated video-generation speed and quality without repetitive sampling.

paragraphs: NeurVLA addresses execution failures in vision-language-action models used for robotic manipulation. These models have shown promise, but mistakes during action execution can hinder their transfer to varied, open-ended tasks. The paper identifies two weaknesses in existing failure handling: corrections that are too coarse and prevention that is insufficiently reliable.

The proposed framework uses neural-symbolic reasoning to address correction and prevention jointly. These are related but distinct responsibilities: correction responds to an execution failure, while prevention concerns avoiding failures before they occur. NeurVLA also internalizes these failure-handling capabilities into the vision-language-action model, making their incorporation into the action model part of the approach itself.

Experiments report strong performance and robust generalization across diverse tasks. The stated findings support the framework's combined treatment of failure response and prevention in the evaluated settings. Its broader significance is the focus on handling execution problems as part of embodied competence: successful transfer involves dealing with what goes wrong during action, alongside producing actions for the original task.
icml-2026-neurvla-unleashing-failure-han.tldr: NeurVLA combines neural-symbolic failure correction and prevention and incorporates those capabilities into robotic vision-language-action models.

paragraphs: PrivCode++ studies private code generation when both instructions and their corresponding code contain sensitive information. Earlier differentially private approaches primarily protected code while treating prompts as public. The paper argues that this assumption misses realistic cases and that removing access to sensitive prompts can sharply reduce generation utility, diversity, and fidelity.

The proposed solution is a two-stage differentially private framework with a Privacy-Free Latent Conditioning module. This module enables effective private fine-tuning and data synthesis without direct access to sensitive prompts or code. The central design question is how to preserve useful conditioning for code generation while extending the privacy scope to both parts of an instruction–code pair.

Experiments report substantially higher utility than baselines and competitive performance with a method that relaxes privacy assumptions. PrivCode++ also provides stronger privacy guarantees in the comparison described. The contribution is therefore a combination of broader protection and improved usefulness under that protection, addressing the utility loss that arises when sensitive prompts cannot be used directly during generation.
icml-2026-privcode-latent-conditioned-di.tldr: PrivCode++ uses latent conditioning to improve differentially private code generation while treating both prompts and code as sensitive.

paragraphs: R³DAO addresses long data-science workflows in which later steps depend strongly on earlier ones. Static execution chains can let an early error propagate until the overall task fails. The framework instead uses execution feedback to revise the organization of the workflow, with the aim of recovering locally and improving efficiency over time.

A dynamic hierarchical task network breaks the overall intent into high-level logical anchors and smaller operations. When execution produces anomalies, semantic reflection converts them into diagnostic signals that guide local changes to the task structure. This replaces costly global resets with targeted reconstruction. A further experience-distillation process compresses long trajectories into structured prior information to guide subsequent execution.

On MLE-bench, the paper reports a 77.36% improvement in success rate over R&D-Agent while maintaining competitive task scores. It also reports a 36-fold reduction in average execution time and token consumption of 104,000 per task. These findings support feedback-driven restructuring as a way to improve reliability and resource use in the evaluated long-horizon workflows.
icml-2026-r-3-dao-reactive-recovery-and-.tldr: R³DAO uses execution feedback, local workflow reconstruction, and distilled experience to improve long-horizon data-agent reliability and efficiency.

paragraphs: TGV-KV reduces the memory used by vision-language models during autoregressive generation. These models cache token keys and values to speed up subsequent steps, but cache size grows with context length. Visual tokens can contain substantial redundancy, and eviction policies designed for text models may discard information poorly when applied across both modalities.

The method uses textual guidance to judge which visual information matters. Text-Vision Budgeting allocates cache capacity across layers based on mutual-information interactions. Text-Weighted Ranking assesses text priority and ranks visual tokens through weighted text–image attention. Text-Prioritised Retention then preserves text keys and values strategically to avoid sharp information loss.

Evaluation covers five models with different sizes and architectures. For LLaVA-NeXT on VizWiz-VQA, the paper reports retaining 99.2% of full-cache accuracy with a 5% retention budget, alongside a 52.6% increase in end-to-end throughput. This is relative preservation of the full-cache result, not an absolute accuracy of 99.2%. The findings show that modality-aware cache choices can preserve useful information even under aggressive memory reduction.
icml-2026-tgv-kv-text-grounded-kv-evicti.tldr: TGV-KV uses text-guided budgeting, ranking, and retention to shrink vision-language model caches while preserving accuracy in evaluated settings.

paragraphs: This paper tests whether publicly available LoRA modules can be recycled effectively through adaptive merging. Such methods select modules from a pool and tune their mixing coefficients using task-specific data. The study uses nearly 1,000 user-contributed LoRAs based on Llama 3.1 8B-Instruct, examining a repository-derived pool rather than only specially assembled modules.

The authors compare adaptive and non-adaptive merging approaches, including a new method developed through a broad methodological search. Adaptive merging improves on the base model, but offers limited benefit over training a fresh LoRA with the same data used to tune the merging coefficients. In the study, the particular modules selected matter little, and randomly initialized LoRA parameters produce similar performance.

Those findings question how much useful prior task knowledge is being recovered in this setting. However, the paper also confirms positive transfer when the pool contains highly relevant LoRAs. Its conclusion is therefore conditional: recycling can help with suitable source modules, but gains over a base model alone do not establish an advantage over directly training a new adapter.
icml-2026-the-appeal-and-reality-of-recy.tldr: Recycling repository LoRAs offers limited gains over training a fresh adapter in this study, although highly relevant modules can provide positive transfer.

paragraphs: This paper frames high-resolution visual reasoning as a problem of acquiring the right evidence under limited perceptual capacity. A broad view preserves context but loses fine detail, so answering a difficult question may require decisions about where to inspect next. The authors formalize those decisions through sequential Bayesian optimal experimental design.

Exact Bayesian inference is intractable in continuous gigapixel image spaces, so the method derives a tractable objective balancing coverage and resolution as a proxy for task-relevant information gain. The resulting procedure, FOVEA, refines crop proposals from a vision-language model through evidence-oriented probing. It requires no training and treats visual inspection as a sequence of purposeful information-gathering steps.

Experiments on high-resolution benchmarks report consistent gains over direct answering and ReAct-style baselines, with especially strong improvements in remote-sensing tasks dominated by search. These results support the value of managing what the model examines before asking it to decide. The computationally practical objective remains a proxy for information gain, rather than an exact solution to the underlying Bayesian inference problem.
icml-2026-the-perceptual-bandwidth-bottl.tldr: FOVEA improves high-resolution visual reasoning through training-free, sequential crop refinement guided by a tractable proxy for information gain.

paragraphs: DualUCOD detects camouflaged objects without pixel-level training labels. Existing approaches generate substitute labels from visual features, but noisy labels can teach incorrect information, and their supervision may be insufficient for detailed segmentation. The paper addresses both the initial quality of these pseudo-labels and the refinement needed to recover object boundaries.

Its spectral pseudo-labeling strategy combines semantic and color cues in an affinity matrix that represents relationships within an image. Eigenvectors of the normalized graph Laplacian are then used to generate pseudo-labels. A boundary-guided foreground–background module adds explicit boundary information to improve segmentation accuracy beyond the initial labels.

A dual-branch contrastive module supplies another learning signal using original and augmented images. It constructs positive and negative pairs, bringing positive representations together while separating them from negatives. Together, the components combine better substitute supervision, boundary refinement, and representation learning. Experiments across different datasets report improvements over state-of-the-art methods in the unsupervised setting. The findings support this combined approach to learning concealed object structure without pixel-level annotations.
icml-2026-unsupervised-camouflaged-objec.tldr: DualUCOD combines spectral pseudo-labels, boundary refinement, and contrastive learning to improve camouflaged-object segmentation without pixel-level labels.

paragraphs: ViEEG decodes visual information from EEG recordings using a representation inspired by hierarchical processing in the visual cortex. The paper argues that flat neural representations overlook this organization. It therefore separates visual stimuli into contour, foreground object, and contextual scene components, which anchor three corresponding streams of an EEG encoder.

The streams are progressively combined through cross-attention routing, following an intended progression from lower-level to higher-level visual information. Hierarchical contrastive learning then aligns the EEG representations with CLIP representations. This alignment enables zero-shot object recognition, connecting measured neural activity to a visual representation space through multiple levels of structure.

Experiments on THINGS-EEG report large improvements over previous methods in both subject-dependent and subject-independent settings. Results on THINGS-MEG further support generalization to another neural measurement modality. The contribution is an explicit hierarchy for organizing and combining visual information in neural decoding. The architecture is inspired by cortical organization, while the reported evidence establishes improvements in decoding performance across the evaluated datasets and settings.
icml-2026-vieeg-hierarchical-visual-neur.tldr: ViEEG organizes EEG decoding around contours, objects, and scenes, improving zero-shot visual recognition through hierarchical representation alignment.

paragraphs: WeDLM aims to turn the parallel decoding potential of diffusion language models into practical speed improvements. Recovering multiple masked tokens per step can offer parallelism, but bidirectional attention often prevents standard prefix key–value caching. That incompatibility helps explain why some diffusion approaches fail to outperform optimized autoregressive inference engines.

The framework retains standard causal attention through Topological Reordering. Observed tokens move to the physical prefix while keeping their logical positions, allowing masked positions to condition on all observed tokens. A streaming procedure then continually commits confident tokens into a growing left-to-right prefix. This avoids the stop-and-wait pattern associated with block-based diffusion decoding.

Experiments report preserved quality relative to strong autoregressive backbones, with speedups approaching threefold on difficult reasoning benchmarks and reaching tenfold in low-entropy generation settings. Comparisons use autoregressive baselines served by vLLM under matched deployment conditions. The results show that compatibility with caching and continuous decoding can make parallel token recovery practically useful, with the size of the speedup depending on the generation regime.
icml-2026-wedlm-reconciling-diffusion-la.tldr: WeDLM combines reordered causal attention with streaming diffusion decoding to achieve practical speedups while retaining prefix caching and evaluated generation quality.
